body:
Part of [Map: tigerstore, a faster etcd for Kubernetes on TigerBeetle](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/1).

## Question
Which test layers exist, and which of them gate a release?

## Context
From [Test tools for etcd-API correctness, k8s e2e and chaos](https://github.com/djosh34/tigerstore/issues/5): no ready-made suite certifies an etcd endpoint. Reusable layers: (1) the kube-apiserver etcd3 storage tests through a test-server adapter, as kine does; (2) etcd's robustness traffic, model and Porcupine checker, ported away from etcd process control and WAL reading; (3) full Kubernetes conformance with Hydrophone on kind with external etcd, 1 to 2 hours; (4) chaos with tc netem (loss, corruption, delay, jitter, reordering, duplication), full partitions and SIGKILL of node processes, with the linearizability checker running during the faults and durability checks after healing; (5) Jepsen's etcd suite, which needs porting and is amd64-only stock.

## Options
A. Layers 1 to 4 on every PR where they fit in time, all of them gate the release. No Jepsen.
B. A plus a Jepsen port.
C. Layers 1 and 3 only.

## Recommendation
A. Unit tests and layer 1 on every PR, layer 2 and short chaos runs on every PR, full conformance and long chaos runs (for example 1 hour) nightly and before a release. A checker timeout or a skipped check counts as a failure, not a pass.

comments.body: Owner reply, round 2 (not final): leans A, but wants full control over the faults: own TCP or UDP proxies that drop, delay, corrupt and reorder. Asked why the suites need porting when we speak the etcd API. Re-asked in round 3.

Owner answer, round 3: A. Our own seeded Go fault proxy on every link (client to tigerstore, tigerstore to tigerstore, TigerBeetle to TigerBeetle) is the main chaos tool: drop, delay, stall, reset, corrupt and duplicate bytes, one-way and full partitions. tc netem adds real packet loss and reordering. Layers: apiserver storage tests, ported etcd linearizability checker, full conformance, chaos with the checker running. All gate the release. No Jepsen. Every PR: layers 1 and 2 plus a short chaos run. Nightly and before release: full conformance and long chaos runs. A checker timeout or skipped check is a failure.

title: Test layers and the release gate
